transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

I just... I came in because my sleep is just, it's all broken up now. I get off my overnight shift at the care home and I go home and just lie there wide awake. It doesn't help that the bus ride back is always so loud. I take the 42, and it's always packed, and the brakes squeak so bad at every single stop. I told the driver once that he needs to get them checked, but he just looked at me weird. People look at me weird a lot lately, I don't know why. 

But anyway, I just stare at the ceiling for hours, and then when I actually do drift off, I wake up so scared. Like, my heart is just pounding out of my chest. And then I have to get up for my next shift and I feel like I never rested at all. Mrs. Higgins—she's one of my ladies at the home, I help her with her meals and stuff—she said I look like a zombie. She always wants her tea at 3 AM, even though she never actually drinks it, she just lets it sit there and get cold... what was I saying? Oh, yeah, just... I can't sleep right.
When you're trying to sleep, do you find yourself thinking about things over and over, or feeling anxious about something?

I try not to think about things, but... yeah. I just lay there and my brain just starts playing this highlight reel of every single mistake I've ever made. Like, every little thing I did wrong with my patients, or even with my family back when we actually talked. I remember this one time I accidentally gave Mr. Peterson the wrong flavor of pudding—he wanted vanilla but I gave him butterscotch—and he got so upset, he threw the cup at the wall. The stain is still there, right above the baseboard. The maintenance guy, Gary, said he was gonna paint over it, but he never did. Gary's always saying he'll do things and then he just disappears for hours. I think he sleeps in his truck out back. 

But anyway, when I'm lying in bed, it's just... it feels like I'm a completely worthless aide. Like I don't deserve to be taking care of these people. And I just get this heavy, awful feeling that God is furious with me. Like He's mad that I'm not protecting people better. I used to go to church with my grandma when I was little—St. Jude's, over on 4th Street. They had these big stained glass windows that always looked so pretty when the sun came through, but it was always freezing in there. I always had to wear a sweater, even in July. But yeah... I just feel like God is punishing me for being so useless.
Do you often feel guilty or like you're a bad person, even when others don't seem to think so?

Yeah, all the time. Like I was just saying, I just keep going over every single little thing I ever did wrong with my patients, or with my family. It just plays on a loop in my head. I really do feel like I'm a completely worthless aide, and I just know God is mad at me for not protecting people better. I'm supposed to be keeping them safe, you know? 

But it's so hard to keep them safe when the building is falling apart. Like, the handle on the back patio door is completely busted, anyone could just walk right in. I told my supervisor, Brenda, about it like three weeks ago. Brenda always wears these really loud high heels that click-clack down the linoleum hallway, so you can always hear her coming from a mile away. She buys them at this discount shoe place out by the highway, the one right next to the old diner that got shut down last year. I used to get strawberry milkshakes there when I was in high school, back before I dropped out. They had the best whipped cream, they actually made it from scratch in the back... wait, what did you ask me? 

Oh. Right, feeling like a bad person. Yeah, I just... I feel like I'm failing everybody.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah... I don't really do anything anymore. Most days I feel heavy and empty from the minute I open my eyes. It's like the person who used to go to church, and do Zumba, and help the kids at the center is just... gone. 

I used to love going to the community center. We had these big plastic bins of wooden blocks, and this one little boy, Leo, he used to make these huge towers. He'd stack them all the way up to his chin and then just smash them down. It was so loud, but he thought it was the funniest thing in the world. The floor in that room is made of that weird squishy rubber stuff, you know? Like they put at playgrounds now so kids don't get hurt when they fall. When I was little, playgrounds just had woodchips, and you'd always get splinters in your hands and your knees. I got a huge splinter once and my grandma had to dig it out with a sewing needle. She kept all her sewing stuff in this blue metal butter cookie tin. You know the ones? You'd open it up hoping for a cookie, but it was always just thread and buttons and thimbles... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Enjoying things. Yeah, I just... I don't have it in me anymore. I just feel empty.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. Like I said before, most days I just feel heavy and empty from the minute I open my eyes. It's like the person who used to go to church, and do Zumba, and help the kids at the center is just... gone. 

Zumba used to be so fun. The instructor, Maria, she always wore these bright neon pink leggings that you could probably see from space. She had this huge water bottle covered in stickers—one of them was this little cartoon avocado lifting weights. I tried eating avocados for a while because everyone said they were a superfood, but they just taste like wet grass to me. My grandma used to make this amazing guacamole though, she put a ton of garlic in it. We'd eat it with those salty tortilla chips, the ones in the yellow bag. The last time I bought a bag of those, half of them were crushed at the bottom. It's so annoying when you buy a bag of chips and it's mostly just air and crumbs. I ended up just throwing them away because you can't even dip the crumbs, they just fall right into the bowl... 

But yeah, I don't know. I just feel heavy all the time.
Have you ever felt like life isn't worth living, or had thoughts about not wanting to be alive?

Yeah... I think about dying a lot, honestly. Especially when I'm driving home in the morning after my shift. I just stare at the road and wish I could just not wake up, or just disappear, you know? Like, if I wasn't here, everybody would be safer without me. 

Driving in the morning is the worst anyway because the sun is right in your eyes. My visor is broken in my car—it's a '98 Corolla, the silver kind where the paint is all peeling off the hood. I bought it from this guy on Craigslist who smelled like stale cigarettes and peppermint, which is such a weird combination. He had this little dog, a pug I think, that just kept snorting the whole time I was signing the title. Pugs are so cute but they always sound like they can't breathe. My neighbor growing up had a pug named Buster, and Buster used to dig under the fence and get into our garden. He completely ruined my mom's tomato plants one summer. She was so mad, she had spent all spring tying them up to those wooden stakes with little pieces of pantyhose. She said pantyhose was the best thing to use because it stretches and doesn't cut into the plant stems. She used to wear pantyhose to church every Sunday, the really shiny kind that makes that swishing sound when you walk...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh. Yeah, I just... I wish I could just disappear so everyone would be safe.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

I haven't really noticed. I guess I just eat whenever. But honestly, I don't even think about food much anymore. I just... I don't know. 

I used to love going to the grocery store though. The one down the street from me has this bakery section right when you walk in, and it always smells like fresh bread and those sugar cookies with the thick frosting. The frosting is always neon pink or yellow, and it's so sweet it almost hurts your teeth. I used to buy those cookies for the kids at the center when it was someone's birthday. We'd put these little plastic rings on top of them, like spider rings for Halloween or little dinosaurs. Dinosaurs are so weird when you think about it. Like, giant lizards just walking around everywhere. My little brother was obsessed with them when we were kids. He had this huge plastic T-Rex that he carried everywhere, even to bed. One time he left it on the floor in the hallway and my dad stepped on it in the middle of the night. He yelled so loud it woke the whole house up. My dad always wore these thick wool socks around the house because his feet were always cold. He said it was bad circulation, but I think our house was just drafty. The windows in the living room used to rattle whenever the wind blew hard...

What was the question? Sorry. I just... I don't really pay attention to what I eat.
